what: The shape every result.json must have. Validated by the readers, not by the generator.
why: A generator that checks its own output can only confirm it agrees with itself.
This file is checked by the processes that consume the fixtures — the Python and Rust readers — so a field dropped from the generator fails in places the edit that dropped it never touched.
A check that can be deleted by the same motion that deletes what it checks is not a check.

required.what: string — one sentence saying what this vector is for
required.cites: array of strings, non-empty — sections and numbered decisions of docs/replicated-tables.md that this vector exercises
required.converges: boolean — whether the two directions must produce identical dumps
required.stable: boolean — whether merging a second time must change nothing
required.ab: object — the merge result of B into A
required.ba: object — the merge result of A into B

requiredInResult.applied: integer — rows inserted that were not held before
requiredInResult.duplicate: integer — rows already held with the same content
requiredInResult.rejected: array of strings — row ids refused, in the _r_parents text form

optional.shrinksAt: string — when a stated limitation stops applying
optional.pairedWith: string — the runtime test holding the other half of this property, so deleting either half is visible from the one that remains

note: A reader that finds a missing or misshapen field must fail rather than skip: a vector it cannot understand is a vector it is not checking, and a silent skip is indistinguishable from a pass.
